result.title: World Models Favor Learned Priors over Visual Evidence
result.summary: World models are increasingly used to simulate physical interactions, but training a separate model for each environment limits scalability. Cross-environment prediction requires identifying the current physical rule, which appearance alone may not reveal. We therefore study visual calibration: using object motion and interactions in a short video as direct evidence to infer the current rule and predict motion under that rule from a different initial state. However, differences in data availability across physical conditions can yield a long-tailed training distribution, biasing models toward common rules even when evidence supports rare ones. To study this challenge, we introduce TailWorld, which evaluates the transfer of demonstrated rules across initial states while independently controlling training imbalance and calibration informativeness. The benchmark compares predictions with two reference futures from the same prediction initial state, one following the demonstrated rule and the other a common rule, to measure prediction bias toward common dynamics. We further propose Rule Inference for Transfer (RIFT), which learns how different rules affect object motion, infers the current rule from calibration interactions, and applies it to prediction from a new initial state. RIFT explicitly controls the influence of training frequency on rule inference, allowing sufficiently informative observational evidence to support rare rules. Experiments on TailWorld show that RIFT improves prediction accuracy and physical consistency across varying training imbalances and distribution shifts, with gains in predicting rare dynamics.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究跨环境世界模型中的「视觉校准」：用短视频中的物体运动与交互作为证据推断当前物理规则，并迁移到新初始状态预测；提出 TailWorld 基准，以「演示规则」和「常见规则」两条参考未来来度量预测向常见动力学的偏向，以及 RIFT 方法显式控制训练频率对规则推断的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「视觉证据 vs 学习先验」的偏向诊断与 RIFT 对训练频率的显式控制，可能对应 LVR 中视觉细节是否真正进入推理状态、长尾或语言先验压制证据的问题，可供核查作为缓解视觉旁路的线索。
